subject: RELEASE statement
notes: RULE (`--check 14.9.32.4 "The execution of a RELEASE statement causes the record named by record-name-1 to be released to the initial phase of a sort operation."` => OK 14.9.32.4 2). WHAT THE CODE DOES: SortEmitter.EmitRelease renders record-name-1's own character image and calls `CobolSort.Release(sd, image)`, which appends it to that SD's per-file image buffer in release order (CobolSort.cs:77) -- the buffer the SORT's sequence phase then orders and the RETURN phase drains, i.e. exactly the initial phase. The image is a C# string, so the store holds a snapshot: a later mutation of the record area cannot alter an already-released record. THREE LENGTH SHAPES READ AND VERIFIED, all three per 13.18.43.4 GR13 (`--check 13.18.43.4 "During the execution of a RELEASE, REWRITE, or WRITE statement, the number of bytes in the record is determined by the following conditions"` => OK 13.18.43.4 13): (a) fixed SD -- the named record's own width (probe out-b1/probe/base/base.cob returns AAAaaaaa / BBBbbbbb / CCCccccc in key order); (b) RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON -- GR13a's length, emitted as `StrRefMod(image, 1, (int)dep)` (`--check 13.18.43.4 "If data-name-1 is specified, by the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1."` => OK 13.18.43.4 13) a)); (c) GR13c, a variable-occurrence record with no DEPENDING ON in the RECORD clause -- probe out-b1/probe/odo/odo.cob generates `CobolSort.Release("RELODO::SRTF", SRT_REC.AsImage().Substring(0, CobolTable.OdoExtentChars(CobolTable.Occ(WS_OCC), 1, 9, 6, 2, 1)))`, i.e. fixed portion 6 + 2 occurrences x 2 = 10 bytes, not the maximum. COVERING TEST is spec-derived (AssertSpec with expectations computed from the standard, not from the legacy oracle) and cites 14.9.32 GR2 in its own section header. EDITIONS: Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32; the rule is edition-neutral in its own text.
